question: Q4 / Q1
trigger_or_metric: Culinary among topics often searched for on social media
population: Jakpat online panel (self-selected app users), various regions of Indonesia
proxy_note: Search topic, not a visit or purchase trigger; multiple-answer (entertainment 62%, culinary 59%, travel 54%)
snippet: Setelah hiburan, kuliner (59%) dan traveling (54%) menjadi topik yang paling banyak dicari berikutnya.
notes: Relay (GoodStats) of a Jakpat survey; Jakpat original not found. Category label 'kuliner'. Qualitative sentence in the same article: 'Banyak pengguna yang sebelum memutuskan untuk mencoba makanan tertentu atau berkunjung ke suatu tempat, akan melihat ulasan (review) dari food vlogger atau travel influencer terlebih dahulu' - no percentage given for this behaviour (gap).

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Reasons to try a new eating place: good reviews/ratings (ulasan/peringkat bagus)
base_n: 769 (this article; other GoodStats/Jakpat pieces and rows P4W1-R04 to R07 give 995)
population: Jakpat respondents who usually eat out, eight Java cities (Jakarta not included)
proxy_note: Java urban proxy; Jakarta not in sample
snippet: Adapun faktor lainnya mencakup media sosial/iklan (44%), lokasi yang strategis (43%), dan ulasan/peringkat bagus (42%).
notes: Same Jakpat survey as rows P4W1-R04 to R07 and UA-N60 to UA-N67 but a different item (reasons to try a new place). Base conflict: this GoodStats article says 769 respondents, others say 995; the 995 may be the full sample and 769 the eat-out subset (not confirmed). Ratings/reviews rank sixth among reasons, below price 64%, unique menu 49%, opening promo 48%, social media/ads 44%, location 43%. No minimum-rating threshold reported.

question: Q4 / H1
trigger_or_metric: Would try eating at a new place (share choosing to try a new place)

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Share influenced by product links shared by creators (and by platform-led promotions)
ref_period: impact.com x Cube 2025 edition; trade-press article 2025-07-30
base_n: Over 2,400 consumers, creators and industry experts in six SEA markets; base for this item not stated
population: Mixed (consumers, creators, experts), six SEA markets
proxy_note: The article does not say whether 31% and 30% are Indonesia or the six-market total; treat as regional
snippet: with 31% of consumers influenced by product links shared by creators and 30% by platform-led promotions - both outperforming brand ads or influencer posts that don’t include direct purchase links.
notes: Same relay article as existing row P4W2-01 (single outlet; impact.com original behind a form). Items are 'influenced by', not purchase rates. Category not food-specific (article names beauty and fashion as leading categories).

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Micro and nano influencers vs larger tiers: resilience of trust
value: qualitative: micro and nano influencers are weathering the drop in trust better; gap between tiers narrowed
ref_period: impact.com x Cube 2025 edition; trade-press article 2025-07-30
base_n: Over 2,400 respondents in six SEA markets; Indonesia n not given
population: Mixed (consumers, creators, experts), six SEA markets
proxy_note: Qualitative statement in a regional study; no Indonesian micro-vs-mega conversion figure printed
snippet: micro and nano influencers - who typically have closer, more community-like relationships with their followers - are weathering the drop in trust better than their larger counterparts. This has narrowed the gap between influencer tiers, the study concluded.
notes: Same article also says: in Indonesia 'celebrity and mega influencers dominate the landscape' and 'all other influencer tiers in Indonesia also outperform the regional benchmark'; 59% of SEA respondents are influenced by mega influencers (>1m followers), a 7% drop (unit not stated). Direction: weakly supports micro creators for CORSA, but no conversion data. Disconfirming-ish: celebrities and mega creators still lead in Indonesia.

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Indonesian beauty buyers who trust peer reviews (UGC) more than influencer content
base_n: Over 6,000 consumers across Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore; Indonesia n not given
population: Consumers (beauty/makeup category), Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore
proxy_note: Beauty/makeup category, not F&B; use only as a proxy for peer reviews vs influencers
snippet: Among Indonesian respondents, 54% said they trust peer reviews more than influencer content
notes: Relay (Marketing-Interactive); YouGov original ('From Screen to Shelves') not opened. 54% is the highest of the three countries; the other 46% are not split (could trust influencers more or neither). Disconfirms the idea that influencers beat peers on trust, within beauty.

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Trust peer reviews over influencers: high-income vs lower-income consumers (beauty)
base_n: Over 6,000 consumers in three countries; group n and income cut-offs not given
population: Consumers (beauty/makeup category), Indonesia
proxy_note: Beauty/makeup category; income definitions not printed
snippet: Among high-income consumers in Indonesia, 62% place greater trust in UGC, compared to just 33% among lower-income groups.
notes: Relevant to the affluent SCBD segment (peer reviews matter more with income) but the proxy is beauty. Income-group definitions are not stated in the article.

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Favour live formats for beauty content: Indonesian millennials vs Gen Z
base_n: Over 6,000 consumers in three countries; generation n not given
population: Indonesian millennials and Gen Z (beauty category)
proxy_note: Beauty/makeup category; generation boundaries not printed
snippet: While 27% of Indonesian millennials favour live formats, only 18% of Gen Z say the same.
notes: One of the few explicit generation splits found for Indonesia (proxy category). Same article: 'nearly a third of all Indonesian respondents tune in regularly to beauty livestreams', 94% of those viewers made purchases during sessions.

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Generational pattern of pre-purchase information source (online shopping): Gen Z influencers, Millennials reviews, Gen X family/friends
population: Indonesian online shoppers by generation
canonical_band: Gen Z; Younger/Older Millennials; Gen X
proxy_note: General online shopping, not F&B; relay without figures; YouGov original not opened
snippet: Riset terbaru YouGov mengungkap pola unik: Generasi Z lebih dipengaruhi influencer , Milenial banyak mengandalkan ulasan produk, sementara Gen X percaya pada rekomendasi keluarga atau teman.
notes: Relay (marketing.co.id, a trade outlet); no numbers, base or fieldwork date; treat as a lead, tier 3 and weak. Supports the idea that 25-39 Millennials lean on reviews and ratings rather than influencers (Gen Z) or family (Gen X). Page also states 'rating bintang lima ... ukuran keandalan' for Millennials but without data.

question: Q4 / H1

ref_period: impact.com x Cube x Dentsu 2026 edition; Pasardana article 2026-07-27
base_n: 2,400 consumers, six SEA markets (Indonesia n not given)
population: Consumers in Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Philippines
proxy_note: Regional total, not Indonesia-only; score scale described as influence out of 4
snippet: rekomendasi dari keluarga dan teman tetap menjadi sumber yang paling dipercaya dalam pengambilan keputusan pembelian, dengan responden memberikan skor 2,42 dari 4 untuk tingkat pengaruhnya, mengungguli ulasan daring (2,36) dan kreator (1,98).
notes: Relay (Pasardana) of a press release; original impact.com report not opened. Direction: against H1 as 'main trigger' (friends/family and online reviews rank above creators), but the gap between friends and reviews is small (difference not stored as a row). Single outlet read.

notes: Ever-purchased measure (no period), regional. The Indonesia counterpart (76% via creator-linked content) is in P4W2-01; Indonesia 76% vs regional 67% comes from different editions (2025 vs 2026) and wording.

question: Q4

ref_period: impact.com x Cube x Dentsu 2026 edition; Pasardana article 2026-07-27

snippet: Vietnam (34%) dan Indonesia (31%) memimpin kawasan dalam penggunaan AI generatif untuk penemuan produk
notes: Competing discovery channel to creators and Maps. Same article: 40% say generative AI did not change how much they rely on creators for recommendations. Regional total 24% use AI tools in the shopping journey.

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Affiliate links: opened a link (traffic) vs purchased through one in the last six months
base_n: 1,714 (this article; the linked Jakpat report page says 2,125)
population: Jakpat respondents across Indonesia
proxy_note: Not food-specific; Jakpat panel
snippet: Affiliate links are highly effective at driving traffic, evidenced by 83% of consumers who have opened them. However, converting that curiosity into actual sales poses its own challenge, as less than 40% of consumers made a purchase within the last half-year.
notes: Jakpat original page opened. Base conflict (1,714 here vs 2,125 on the referenced report page). Article also says purchase rates are about 40% across genders and generations and drop sharply among low-income consumers. Disconfirming: high reach, modest conversion.

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Live shopping: routinely watch; purchased in last six months; by generation
value: 92 (routinely watch); more than half purchased within six months; Millennials 59, Gen X 58, Gen Z 51 (prefer watching)
population: Jakpat respondents across Indonesia
canonical_band: Gen Z; Younger/Older Millennials; Gen X
proxy_note: Not food-specific
snippet: the vast majority of consumers routinely watching these sessions (92%). This high engagement rate drives instant, real-world action, as proven by more than half of the respondents making a purchase within the last six months. Demographically, women constitute the largest group making purchases through live shopping (62%). Meanwhile, Millennials (59%) and Gen X (58%) prefer watching these sessions more than Gen Z (51%).
notes: Exact label for generation figures is 'prefer watching these sessions'; base of the percentages per generation is not stated. Reasons printed: promotions and discounts 71%, cheaper prices 66%, ability to ask the seller 65%; Gen Z focuses more on reviews, tips, comparisons. Shopee Live used by about 3 in 4, TikTok Live 56%. Direction: live commerce is mainstream but promo-driven; no food split.

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Live shopping: purchase rate (ever bought in a live session), time series
value: 46 (1H 2024); 44 (2H 2025). Also awareness 80 (2H 2024) and 85 (1H 2025); ever joined a live session 74 (1H 2024) and 79 (2H 2025)
population: Jakpat respondents, Indonesia
proxy_note: Not food-specific; sample sizes per wave not printed
snippet: reaching 80% in the second half of 2024, and continuing to rise to 85% in the first half of 2025. [...] In the first half of 2024, 74% of consumers stated that they had ever joined a live session, growing to 79% in the second half of 2025. Although the purchase rate experienced a slight fluctuation from 46% in the first half of 2024 to 44% in the second half of 2025
notes: Period labels are half-years (1H/2H) as printed. Flat purchase rate despite rising awareness and participation: live commerce is not growing in conversion. Wave bases not printed.

question: Q4 / H1
trigger_or_metric: Coffee: trusted source when looking for coffee product information - recommendations from closest people
ref_period: Jakpat coffee survey 2025; article 2025-07-04 (fieldwork dates not printed)
population: Jakpat respondents, Indonesia (coffee survey)
proxy_note: Coffee product choice, not venue choice; multiple-answer item
snippet: When looking for information about coffee products, the majority of people trust recommendations from the closest people (57%), followed by TV commercials (38%).
notes: Jakpat original page opened. Instagram is the main digital channel (16%); online ordering apps 8%. Jakpat researcher comment: 'Word of mouth is still the main driver in choosing coffee'. Supports peer referral over creator content for F&B (beverage).

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Indonesia video commerce: transaction volume and active sellers/shops (2025 estimate)
ref_period: e-Conomy SEA 2025 (Google, Temasek, Bain); trade-press article 2025-11-17
population: Indonesia, all video commerce categories
proxy_note: All categories, not F&B; relay of the Google/Temasek/Bain report; Indonesia-specific breakdown not in the Bain press release
snippet: transaction volumes surged 90% year on year to 2.6 billion, alongside a 75% jump in active sellers and online shops, reaching 800,000 in total.
notes: Relay (Marketing-Interactive) tier 3; e-Conomy Indonesia chapter not opened. Same article: Indonesia on track for nearly US$100 billion digital GMV in 2025; e-commerce projected +14% to US$71 billion. No F&B split of video commerce. The Bain press release (opened, 2025-11-11) gives only the regional figure: video commerce about 25% of total SEA e-commerce GMV.

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Google Maps ratings and reviews of two Surakarta restaurants vs customer trust and brand loyalty (SEM-PLS)
value: qualitative: positive and significant effect on customer trust (both restaurants); no rating threshold or reading share reported
ref_period: Published 2026-01-30 (journal issue Jan 2026); data collection date not checked
population: Restaurant visitors in Surakarta (Dapur Solo, Mang Engking) who had read or given Google Maps ratings/reviews, aged 17+; purposive sampling
proxy_note: Surakarta (not Jakarta); respondents pre-selected as users of Google Maps reviews; 44.5% aged 21-25, 28.5% aged 26-30
snippet: data collected from 400 respondents who have visited the selected restaurants and interacted with Google Maps ratings and reviews. The results reveal that Google Maps ratings and reviews have a positive and significant effect on customer trust in both restaurants.
notes: Peer-reviewed (SENTRI: Jurnal Riset Ilmiah, DOI 10.55681/sentri.v5i1.5565, open access, Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta). Non-probability purposive sample; association only. Selection bias: only people who used Google Maps reviews. No finding on a minimum star rating or on the share who read reviews before visiting (gap).

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: TikTok and Instagram content vs purchase intention of Gen Z for culinary MSMEs in Situbondo
value: qualitative: both positive and significant; TikTok greater than Instagram; R-squared 57.4%
population: Gen Z TikTok/Instagram users in Situbondo; purposive sampling; 5-point Likert; multiple linear regression
proxy_note: Non-metropolitan town; purchase intention (not behaviour); self-report
snippet: A sample of 100 respondents was determined through purposive sampling. [...] with TikTok having a greater influence than Instagram. [...] A coefficient of determination of 57.4% indicates
notes: Peer-reviewed (JPEK, DOI 10.29408/jpek.v10i1.34042, open access). Quote continues: 'TikTok content and Instagram content have a positive and significant effect on purchase intention, with TikTok having a greater influence than Instagram' and 'coefficient of determination of 57.4%'. Non-metropolitan; cannot be generalised to Jakarta 25-39.

question: Q4
trigger_or_metric: Consumer perception of food vlogger reviews after the CB vs Clairmont Bakery case
value: qualitative: trust in influencer reviews fell because of weak transparency and commercial motives; trust remains for honest, consistent, interactive reviewers
population: Online respondents, majority women aged 25-34, highly educated, employed, heavy TikTok/Instagram users; two open questions, thematic analysis
proxy_note: Qualitative, small convenience-type online sample; Jakarta authors, location of respondents not stated
snippet: Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif, data dikumpulkan melalui survey online terhadap 85 responden dengan dua pertanyaan terbuka, lalu dianalisis secara tematik.
notes: Peer-reviewed (Jurnal Pengabdian Masyarakat dan Riset Pendidikan, DOI 10.31004/jerkin.v3i4.1265, SINTA 5). Findings in abstract: 'penurunan kepercayaan terhadap ulasan influencer akibat kurangnya transparansi dan adanya motif komersial'; credibility drivers: sponsor transparency, authentic visuals, social validation from other users. Disconfirming evidence on food-vlogger trust. Closest sample to the CORSA age band (25-34 majority) but n=85 and no sampling frame stated.

question: Q4 / H1
trigger_or_metric: Fear of missing out (FOMO) and reference group effect on consumptive behaviour for trendy culinary (students, Ambon)
value: qualitative: FOMO, lifestyle and reference group each positive and significant on consumptive behaviour
population: Students of the Faculty of Economics and Business, Pattimura University, Ambon; purposive sampling; PLS-SEM
proxy_note: Student sample in Ambon; behaviour (consumptive culinary), no queue variable; only an indirect proxy for crowd/peer cues
snippet: with a total sample studied of 140 samples.
notes: Peer-reviewed (Manis: Jurnal Manajemen dan Bisnis, open access). Abstract: 'Fear Of Missing Out (FOMO) has a positive and significant effect on consumptive behavior ... Reference Group has a positive and significant effect'. Not about queues; weak external validity for Jakarta professionals.

question: Q4 / H1
trigger_or_metric: Why people queue for viral food: social proof and FOMO (qualitative, Blok M, Jakarta)
value: qualitative: no figure; queues described as social validation that makes the item look more attractive
population: Expert commentary (psychology researchers quoted from BBC); Blok M viral food outlets
proxy_note: News feature with quoted academics, not a survey; no Indonesian queue-conversion data
snippet: Jika Anda terus melihat orang mengantre berulang kali, katanya, pengulangan tersebut dapat membuat perilaku mengantre terasa normal.
notes: Quoted experts: Rachel S. Herz (Brown University) on FOMO and Cathrine Jansson-Boyd (Anglia Ruskin University) on 'bukti validasi sosial', relayed from BBC. Qualitative only; no Indonesian measurement of queues as a purchase trigger was found (gap). Photo caption: queue at a viral snack stall in Blok M, South Jakarta.
